physics_goals.quote: The goal of the LUX detector is to clearly detect (or exclude) WIMPS with a spin independent cross section per nucleon of $2\times 10^{-46}$ cm$^{2}$
value: Detect or exclude WIMPs with a spin-independent cross section per nucleon of 2e-46 cm2
Test low-mass WIMP interpretations of other direct-detection results

summary.plain: LUX was a dark matter detector holding about a third of a tonne of liquid xenon, run from 2013 to 2016 in the same underground hall in South Dakota that LZ uses now. It found no dark matter, and set the tightest limits of its day.
summary.technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC, 370 kg total / 250 kg active, in the Davis Cavern at SURF. WS2013 (85.3 live days, 118 kg fiducial) and WS2014-16 (332.0 live days) gave a combined 3.35e4 kg day exposure and a spin-independent limit of 1.1e-46 cm2 at 50 GeV/c2. Direct predecessor of LZ.
